title: Graphics.Blit Scripts for avatars
details:
(Edit: Added "for avatars" to the post title. VRCGraphics.Blit is available for worlds, but not avatars.)

The Shader Community's Request for Graphics.Blit

- What is Graphics.Blit?

[Graphics.Blit](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Graphics.Blit.html) allows you to copy a source texture into a destination render texture using a shader. Being able to do this allows for shaders to write to render textures in a manner that does not require cameras

----

- Why do we want Graphics.Blit?

Currently shader creators are using cameras and render textures to emulate what Graphics.Blit does. Cameras were not made for this purpose and have a relatively high amount of overhead. On top of this, in order to effectively mimic Graphics.Blit we need two cameras to achieve the same effect. This doesn’t mean Graphics.Blit replaces cameras though, it allows for most use cases to run much quicker.

----

- What uses this camera workaround currently?

[GPU particles](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ui87t55nEmk). Anyone who's experimented with GPU particles knows how much faster these particles run compared to Unity's built in particle system. GPU particles in their current form can run a million particles in [1.43ms](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/419351657743253526/504454404477419520/unknown.png) on the GPU. That's amazing already, but because we have to use cameras, [~0.7ms of CPU time(camera0 and camera1)](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/419351657743253526/504453505285881856/unknown.png) is spent on updating the cameras. Graphics.Blit can bring the CPU time from ~0.7ms to ~0.07ms.

GPU particles are not the only shader which will perform better using Graphics.Blit. Any shader which has uses a 2 camera and render texture setup will be faster using Graphics.Blit. 

            Other use potential cases for Graphics.Blit

* GPU dynamic bones

* Cheap Gaussian blur

* Fluid Simulation

* Grass/Hair Simulation

* Procedurally generating Data

* Virtual Keyboard for mutes

* AI for Shader pets following you around

* Simple games and puzzles. Pong, Flappy bird, and the beginnings of Doom have been done with cameras already

* Worlds with snow dynamic, rain puddles, and water ripples

----

- Why should time be spent on Graphics.Blit when only shader creators will be using it?

Even though this is going to mostly only effect shader creators, everyone benefits from this change. GPU particles have been released to the public for a while and has been the only way for VRChat users to get millions of particle without completely destroying FPS. Graphics.Blit would increase the room for innovation.

----

- What would a Graphics.Blit component from the VRC SDK look like?

We would like to see two scripts added to the SDK, a Blit Controller, and a Blit Component.

The Blit Controller should be a component which can be added to game objects on avatars and worlds. The Blit Controller should also have one input, an array of Blit Components. The purpose of this controller is to handle the order in which each blit is executed. In order for a shader to store stateful information, there need to be two render textures and two blits. The order in which these two blits are run is important, and this controller handle that. The Blit Controller component should run Graphics.Blit for every Blit Component in the array, in order.

The Blit Component should hold two inputs, a source texture and a destination texture. Where is the material at? Well in order to allow shaders to be animated in VRC we think that using the shared material from the mesh renderer on the game object would be ideal. The blit component should have a RunBlit function which takes the mesh renderer’s shared material  and runs Graphics.Blit with the source,destination, and shared material.

Also the RunBlit function should pass a couple extra bits of information to the shader. Namely the game object’s localToWorldMatrix, worldToLocalMatrix, and position. We think this is important because with Graphics.Blit you get no outside information. Some of the existing camera effect require position information. 

We have included a GitHub link which contains a mock implementation of what we think would be the best way to implement this for the use cases we have. It is under the MIT licence so feel free to use anything from our implementation. We want to make this as easy as possible on development time.

Our mock implementation: https://github.com/Merlin-san/Blit-Component

We aren't sure if components update on both PlayerLocal and Player for the local player, but updating more than once per frame should be avoided if that's the case.

----

- Safety System

Currently the render texture/camera work around that we use requires that you are friends with another user in order for that user to see the render texture. This was implemented before the safety system. If Graphics.Blit is implemented, render textures should be either apart of the safety system under "shaders", or its own category under "render textures"

- The shader community,

The current Action menu feels redundant (emojis when there's an emoji button) and cramped.

title: [Feedback] Keep Emote Button

comments.body:
This was the biggest glaring issue I noticed with my initial use. Being on Index, I have my left thumbstick click mapped to my A button, which makes it super easy, quick, and intuitive to toggle gestures on and off.
What used to be one action, now takes two actions, both of which take longer to do. This will be incredibly frustrating. I think the simplest solution would be to maintain a dedicated gesture toggle action which can be mapped through the Steam Input. This would allow a legacy option for those who find the new system to be much harder to control (which goes against one of the base goals of the new system).

any toggle you turn on in the new menu will not only lock it on, but it will sync the parameter for late joiners as well.
toggle sets a parameter to a value and holds it. when toggled off it resets it to 0.
not only that, but because you can send actual animator parameters now, you can set your animator up so, say you use a button (a button does what a toggle does, but doesn't hold it. you press it to momentarily make a parameter a value, then back to 0) to move the animator into a state with a hat on. even if that parameter is now 0 you will still have the had on.
you can do what you want, but much much better using using the action menu, so much better that if you take the time, you can even make a very long animation using music and synced visuals semi synced for late joiners by breaking it into a state machine with many entry points that a later joiner could join and slot right into, as granular as you want to spend the time making it

It feels like they're trying to do too much with such a limited space.  What I expected when using the Action menu was: Press, and BAM, emote toggles all around.  Instead it's a two step action: Press, Emote Toggle Menu and then find the Emote you want (unless it's nested into yet another circle).  
The redundancy of the emojis and putting settings and such when I just want to use the "Action" menu just seems to crowd the fluidity on the user's side.

details:
[Valve Index HMD and Controllers]
While testing the 3.0 avatars, I found what I believe to be a bug with the avatar system. This was found using the Young Boy demo avatar (See picture).
When I went into the expressions, there was a menu with an analog radial wheel for controlling the eyes being open and closed. What I found was that if you have them closed (or any value), you could close the whole action menu and it would persist. However, if you have a value set, and you back out one menu, the animation is reset (the eyes snap back open to default). The value is still shown in the menu, and if you go back it snaps to that value. 
I would think that users would want to be able to "lock" this value and animation so that you could keep your eyes closed, for example. In the Nanachi avatar, there were similar values for the body weight, and those persist. This leads me to wonder if the issue is related to the avatar itself or the system.
Video of Repro:
https://youtu.be/5hPg4esvS6o

details: It's an interesting step in the right direction but I don't think it's a good idea to blend them all together. There's no 100% good way to get pin point accuracy on what kind of expression you want to display. Perhaps if we create borders within the analog wheel for expressions so that it looks like pie slices, we can more accurately execute expressions that we want to show without blending them on from another expression or clumsily trying to remember what is what. Also, as a suggestion, center of wheel is resting face; and the further you push the analog towards an expression, the more intense that expression. Thanks.

(I would suggest each wheel is set to 8 animation slots as this is the equivalent we had in avatar 2.0, 8 hand gestures(emotions) and 8 emotes(dances) I don't know how easy this would be to implement but making the amount of slots a variable would make this default much more flexible)
This is simply to provide the same functionality that avatar 2.0 does, at the same accessible amount of unity knowledge, (the only knowledge that is required for 2.0 is how to make an animation and where to replace the defaults in the override). 
This would also help people who simply want to implement a basic emotion, or replace a dance, without having to learn how to use, or go through the unity animation logic/node system.
And make avatar 3.0 more accessible for people who struggle with these concepts and systems.
It would be naturally limited, but it would make it a lot easier for people who just want to upload an avatar with a couple of different common emotions (Happy, Sad etc) Without having to make a new action controller, expressions menu, stage parameter and then go through linking them all together.
There is a lot of new stuff involved to get Avatar 3.0 avatars to work as intended now. So naturally we need to make the system somewhat accessible, even if it is just a limited quick and dirty default option as suggested. Or people will be put off by it.

comments.body: https://vrchat.canny.io/avatar-30/p/feedback-give-users-costumes-or-outfits-for-stage-parameters

Oh! I also just figured out how epic this could actually be. Users could make a customization menu where you can go from basic to fully customized with a few sliders and toggles. Multiple users would use the same avatars but look completely different, and it would remain that way! It craps on performance ranking obviously (at least until it gets renovated), but it takes avatars to a new level, allowing users to "make their own" avatars without comissioning, asking for a customized version, or learning how to upload their own avatars. This reminds me of a plan I had to make a furry avatar that was completely configurable down to body shape, ear shapes, body colors and patterns, etc with a few preset outfits that can be applied to demonstrate the design.

This would also be very awesome for making avatars more accessible to POC people, because avatars could have skin color sliders (I know its possible now, but needing to fix the skin color after every world hop would likely feel shitty, like being in someone else's body every time you switch worlds). Currently avatar makers have to upload more versions of an avatar to have different skin color options (and they usually don't), so POC people are very limited on avatar choice, and even more limited on what color skin they get when they actually find a darker skin avatar. Being able to save avatar states across worlds would let people choose their actual skin color for their avatars.

I've made a fully colourable Avali avatar that uses 9 parameters for colouring (3 colours with HSV params for each). It's currently very annoying to use it, because the avatar resets to default colours every time you switch worlds or start the game, and it's necessary for people to memorize the values (remember, it's 9 different values) for their colour scheme and manually enter them every time.
If parameters were stored and saved, this wouldn't be a problem, and avatars with high customization would be much more usable.
Nice idea. Avatars 3.0 is a good concept because you don't need to make 1 million avatars of the same thing with different outfits, so why not let the options someone sets stay?

@{5c021357a58d0a7e70c3e515|full_name}: I think they are referring to people of colour as POC and that most avatars are most commonly Caucasian in skin colour meaning it's not good to have to change to their desired skin colour every time they swap worlds.

I'd like to be able to save multiple recolorings of the same avatar as if they're different avatars in my favorites, so I can swap between them easily (and of course, not lose the colorings when changing worlds).  I'd prefer to see this separated from "Expressions" into a dedicated "Customizations" area, so that expression animations remain quick-access, and customizations are all grouped together.  It would also make more sense to display certain customizations as a toggle rather than the icon making them seem like a playing animation (even if they are) for less user confusion.  "Save how I look now and keep it permanently" seems like an important aspect of how players experience avatar customizations.

I fully support this idea! This would be a huge quality of life improvement for 3.0 where you may have advanced setups that take time to customize. I really hope to see this happen in the near future.

details:
When creating a toggle in a submenu, the parameter that controls is must be a stage in both the submenu and main menus stageparams. If the parameter is a stage on only the submenus stageparams the toggle will not function. I've only tested this with buttons and toggles, so I don't know if this happens with any other control type.
The 3.0 avatar walkthrough - part 4 - says though you can make submenus within submenus "And so on. And so on, and so on, and so on… its turtles all the way down, baby!" Forcing a parameter to be featured on both stageparams makes this claim impossible because the stageparams are limited to 16 stages, and the main menus stageparams will quickly be filled by the submenus parameters. So I assume this is a bug.

comments.body:
There must only be one StageParam object you use for your entire avatar. This object must be used in all menus/submenus that you use on that avatar. We may add validation for this in a later version of the SDK.
For using the state of multiple submenus, you can use a single Stage param to indicate "where" in the tree of submenus you are, such as depth.
Alternately, you don't have to set a parameter when you go into a submenu. It is optional.

details:
So we get 16 networked parameters, with each of them being (I assume) a 8-bit unsigned integer, with an option to map it to a floating point value for animator reasons. Avatars with toggleable elements (such as clothing or weapons) are extremely common with avatars 2.0, and avatars 3.0 brings some nice possibilities with it (Sync enabled objects! Perform different actions based on what's active! And more!), and while 16 synced parameters would be perfectly sufficient to support a fair amount of toggles as-is (well, 16 of them, if you don't want any other synced-parameter-driven things), that is certainly a sub-optimal use of a limited resource. At the same time, a single parameter could fit 8 independent binary toggles in it through the power of bit fiddling.
My suggestion, therefore, is to  add the following state behaviors:
 Set parameter bit
  * Parameter name: any int parameter
  * Bit index: which bit to set
  * Bit value (toggle): value to set it to
This one is straightforward. It just changes parameter value. In code, it would be `param |= 1 << index` for set and `param &= ~(1 << index)` for unset.
Change parameter if bit is set
 * Source bitmask: which parameter is tested
 * Source bit index: which bit to check
 * Target parameter: which parameter to change if the bit is set
 * Target value: the value it's changed to
This one would be used to untangle one bitfield parameter into multiple separate parameters. Right now, transition conditions don't have bit test as a comparison type, so with this behavior it would be possible to separate one (synced) bitfield into multiple (unsynced) booleans (or numeric parameters). In code, this would be `if((param & (1 << index)) != 0) target = value`.
Without this, properly handling a bitmask parameter would be hellishly hard, with full 8-depth binary tree of 256 states needing to be mapped out, or all 256 values to be handled manually. This allows a single state to drive 8 individual unsynced parameters on bit field change, and then 8 layers to handle 8 things toggled by 8 unsynced parameters.
In addition, a bit-based control (for setting/resetting bits from actions menu), or the ability to control unsynced parameters (so that they can be used to drive synced values from animation controller afterwards) would be very useful to make better use of these two behaviors.
This would allow creators to squeeze more out of current sync system, enabling avatars with more features and better (possibly) network usage.
title: [FEEDBACK] Add bit operations to available behaviors

comments.body: Alternatively we could just have boolean parameters and have all that bit masking machinery hidden from the user.

So, the whole bitmasking thing is a bit too complex when we're talking about systems we want to expose to potentially amateur creators.
Instead, we've introduced a new system wherein you have 128 bits of space for syncing. Floats and ints take 8, the newly-introduced bools take up 1 bit.
This allows you to do most of what your suggestion requests but with less complexity.
This is available in VRChat 2021.1.1, now in Open Beta. The patch notes are here: https://docs.vrchat.com/v2021.1.1/docs/latest-release#avatars-30
Regardless of this _not entirely being the exact suggestion made_, I'm marking this as complete!

details:
With avatars 2.0, creators are able to use some sort of particle magic (I never learned to use it myself) to control animations on their avatars. I've seen nice examples with people using it to make "realistic" reload for weapons with limited magazine size and the need to pull the magazine far away from the weapon to get it back to full. However, this system depends on particles being enabled (and not hitting particle limits), and is most certainly not synced over network.
With that in mind, it would be nice to implement a system for specifying collider/trigger based events that could change parameters on the main avatar animator (either synced or unsynced). The colliders can be handled only locally, so it would not impact performance of remote players.
A simple example that I could think of is this: let's say an avatar has a pistol in a holster on the hip, and an animation state that would constrain that pistol to avatar's hand. With the proposed system, a completely natural grab interaction can be implemented: a trigger on the holster would set a parameter when a hand enters it, and subsequently triggering the first gesture when that parameter is set would trigger a transition to a state where the pistol is constrained to the hand.
This feature would allow for an amazing variety of immersive interactions and controls. A menu is fine, and the only available control method for some things, but natural lifelike control is a strength of VR.
title: [FEEDBACK] Add collider/trigger based controls

comments.body: This would also be incredibly more optimized, sync better, and easier to use than the "particle magic". We could have working xylophones, keyboards, etc, with very little strain on cpu or net.

With the current control bindings, it's easy to forget that you have the action menu open and hit random gestures when trying to move. One way this could be addressed would be to set up the control bindings so that we could e.g. click the thumbstick to open the action menu, then keep it open as long as the thumbstick capacitative touch sensor is active (this would work for index, oculus, and vive at a minimum).

details:
It would be really amazing if users could store the stage parameters for avatars they have favorited or are currently using (or it can be stored in a secondary local cache that can be cleared). This would essentially a be a menu beside the Expression menu that would allow users to store all of the favorite configurations of any avatar 3.0 avatars you own. This way, you can completely customize your avatar and load that customization on the fly without having to set it up all over again. It could also load whatever outfit they had selected previously when they change back into the avatar, leave, or change worlds until they choose to not wear any of them.

If necessary, in the Params object, users can choose which values are not allowed to be saved (so stage parameters part of a larger sequence don't cause problems).
title: [FEEDBACK] Give users "Costumes" or "Outfits" for stage parameters

comments.body:
Being given presets (or even just keeping the last known values of parameters) would make loading an avatar and calibrating much easier on folks.
Those using generic or elaborate avatars wouldn't have to fumble to get back into a specific style or setup.
I was thinking of mixing together some old avatars that used the same body base, but the fact they wouldn't be able to be saved between worlds kind of spoiled the idea.

details:
When animating non-humanoid bones on the additive layer, like my avatar's wings and tail for example, their rotation ends up offset from how they appear in the Unity editor. A current workaround is to duplicate the provided Locomotion Layer example and add new layers below it, but the AV3 walkthrough and documentation imply that this shouldn't be necessary.
https://youtu.be/SNHVcTvCRmg
title: [BUG] Additive layer offsets the rotation of non-humanoid bones

comments.body:
Updated the documentation on [Additive](https://docs.vrchat.com/v2020.2.3-av3/docs/avatars-30#additive) and [Gesture](https://docs.vrchat.com/v2020.2.3-av3/docs/avatars-30#gesture) to clarify some things. 
Additive should only be used in cases where the bones you're "adding on to" are animated in Base-- by default, only your Mechanim humanoid bones. Since your tail/wings are not animated in Base, you're adding on to nothing, which will result in strange behavior.
Short answer: This isn't a bug! This is us not providing proper documentation. Use Gesture instead for non-humanoid bone "idle" animations.

details:
First of all, amazing job! The amount of work put into that is overwhelming!
Now for feedback and suggestions:
Add AFK icon next to the name plate (like the friend icon) - When using the AFK animation you can't necessarily know if it is the AFK animation or another animation. With AFK icon you can surely know that they are AFK.
Auto AFK on Desktop - Add a feature to auto AFK after a certain amount of time of no key or mouse input.
The "Gestures" section should be moved to config, or another less noticeable location - It is not used as much as the other features and I think it will be better to move it to make place for other more used features.

Could be a good chance to improve Desktop Mode interactions with Avatar 3.0:
Ability to click buttons while holding an object and/or pick a second object simultaneously like in VR Mode - A lot of times I find myself in a situation when I need to drop the object I'm holding to be able to click a button. Also the limitation of Desktop Mode to certain features requires holding 2 objects at the same time. Could be helpful to be able to do that!
The ability to rotate a picked up object while holding a certain key - In Desktop Mode it is very difficult to rotate an object, it requires you to pick up and drop the object in order to rotate it and there's no easy way to rotate items like in VR Mode.
It could be useful to be able to rotate an object while holding a certain key, which disables looking around with the mouse and instead rotate the object.
For example: while holding "T", you can rotate the object with the mouse and when you release it, you can look around again.
That was a bit long lol but I hope you will take any of these suggestions and use them!
Thanks!

details:
To satisfy the use case of controlling a puppet menu while simultaneously locomoting with joysticks, optionally controlling puppet xy (what the joystick would have inputted) instead via relative wrist rotation might work. Basically how smart TVs with accelerometers in the remote control can use that rotation to drive an "air cursor".
I'm thinking it should probably clamp if the wrist is rotated too far, and then as soon as you rotate back the previous max clamp is now the max value and it immediately moves back away from the edge of the puppet dial in that new reference frame.
title: [FEEDBACK] Optionally control puppet xy with wrist rotation

comments.body: I'm certain this is already achievable with the tools we have, but I guess making it more straightforward wouldn't hurt.

@{5b07764455c49e65e1c52311|full_name}: I respectfully disagree. Sure, in Avatar 2.0, we can build many *digital* control tools, and yes we can use FinalIK to control object position, and yes we can use shaders.
The idea of Avatar 3.0 is to allow driving things through the main animator, so there's something compelling about having a set or puppet parameters. For example, driving a 2d blendtree of blend shapes, or controlling a wiggle animation.
I just saw an extremely compelling demo of using wrist rotation as an extremely precise mouse pointer that allows the presenter to position their hand as they choose. 3dof rotation is actually far more precise than the thumbstick or hand position... However, the example I saw was done in SDK2 using a shader. It would be really cool to have the same capability directly through the animator rather than requiring a custom shader.
The canny here is specifically about driving a puppet using wrist rotation, rather than a specific task.

@{5b7c3929d5fc6b20af6b960a|full_name}: I'm in the upvoters, as I don't disagree with adding the implementation, but I also hold the stance that it's already achievable. It's not limited to object rotation either, though that could/would still be a proxy.

details:
I ran into a situation where prone/crouching animations broke, and remained broken until changing worlds. Sample video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iK0kp3v4feY
I suspect (but have not yet verified) that this was caused by the Animator Set View component, locking the viewpoint so that avatar animations cannot force the viewpoint to the ground. This brings multiple bugs to mind:
1. I had attempted to use Set View to move the viewpoint as the avatar scaled, by scaling the avatar root with a radial puppet control, then invoking Animator Set View when the puppet control was closed. However, my viewpoint did not actually change (bug 1?)
2. After this change, desktop crouch/prone animations broke (bug 2?)
3. This broken state was carried over after subsequent avatar changes (this is the biggest issue here).
Note that both SDK2 and 3 avatars were affected to an extent - with SDK2 avatars, the animation was correct but the viewpoint was too high.
Rejoining the instance fixes the issue.
title: [BUG] Broken avatar prone/crouch animations carried over after avatar change

comments.body:
This is a consequence of using the "Set View" state behavior for an unsupported use case. That state behavior is meant to be used for setting your viewpoint after sitting down (as an example), not for use with scaling the avatar.
When using it, you need to be sure to clear it-- as in, run the state behavior again but with the option set to "Clear" or the checkbox empty. There's a bug where some editor scripts will break the Editor UI we're using, so you'll probably just see a checkbox.
Despite what was noted below, we do need to clear "Set View" when swapping into another avatar.

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: Hmm. It's not clear what use cases are intended to be supported by "Set View" in the docs. Reading that "The Animator Set View control allows you to move the viewpoint of the person wearing the avatar to the head at that given point of the animator state." I assumed it would allow me to effectively move the viewpoint position set in the initial avatar descriptor based on the current head bone offset. It would be helpful to clarify in the docs what is and is not intended to be supported with this component.

comments.body: I believe that some of these parameters are implemented but not supported yet (as in they receive no data), but I'll check and put them in.

Upright is extremely important and should be documented: it controls crouch/prone/standing (0 = on floor; 1 = standing upright at calibrated/initial height) The default base crouches at 0.7 and goes prone (crawl) at 0.5
The others, don't seem like they are being used yet.

Supine and GroundProximity are not implemented yet, and will not be documented until they are.
@{5b7c3929d5fc6b20af6b960a|full_name}: LocomotionMode and FootstepDisable were previous properties that we no longer use, and those were left behind in the controller. They do nothing.

Documentation complete!
AngularY and Upright are implemented and has been documented.
Supine and GroundProximity are not implemented yet. This will be documented as "not implemented".
LocomotionMode and FootstepDisable were previous properties that we no longer use, and those were left behind in the default controller. They do nothing and will not be documented.

details:
It would be nice if it were possible to dynamically scale the avatar, adjusting the view position and IPD accordingly.
Currently, there's a "Set View" component, which seems like it would work, but in fact scaling the avatar root the calling "set view" does not in fact adjust the view position or IPD (at least on desktop mode). It's not clear if this use cases is the intended one for "Set View", and this seems like it might have IK side effects as well - so rather than request that "Set View" support this use case, I'd simply like to suggest that this be supported somehow and leave it up to you guys to figure out how best to support this kind of operation.
title: [FEEDBACK] Add support for scaling the avatar, including view position and IPD

comments.body: As a side note, on SDK2 I routinely upload multiple variations of my avatars which differ only in their scale. It would be really nice to not have to do that anymore...!
GoGoLoco's Go Beyond mode has something like this, but only the view position adjusts, not the world scale or IPD, making your controller inputs become misaligned with your armspan.
This post isn't marked as tracked, but the feature is now available in the Open Beta (as of the date of this post)

This was implemented with our Avatar Scaling update!

https://creators.vrchat.com/avatars/avatar-scaling/

details: Even if you use VRC Animator Tracking Control to completely override locomotion animations, I noticed that jumping will partially break it and restore some of your tracking. This is because the jumping animation states in the default Base Layer controller are using VRC Animator Tracking Control. As Tupper pointed in AV3 Walkthrough - Part 3, using VRC Animator Tracking Control in multiple layers leads to unpredictable results, but it's basically required to actually do anything on the Actions Layer. Removing the behavior from the jumping animation states fixes the issue and doesn't seem to cause any problems as far as I was able to test.
title: [FEEDBACK] Remove VRC Animator Tracking Control from the default Base Layer controller

This can be replicated using a custom Action layer that has a state containing an Animation that modifies the root scale and testing the avatar in game. (The Action layer's weight does not need to be set to 1).

details:
Puppet menu is they are best suited to float values. The 2 and 4 Axis puppet make use of the sticks, and the Radial Puppet makes use of a percentage. However, neither of these menus really play well with integers in my testing, so any puppet option better suited for integers would be appreciated.
Additionally, puppet menus use the analog stick for controls, rather than the mouse, or trigger in non-flick select. Meaning the feeling of operating a puppet compared to a button is substantially different.
Not all animations are best suited for working with Float values. Float values work best when working with blendtrees, but for animations that disable or enable certain elements, A float value is only really useful for a transition into a puppet menu.
For example, I have an animation that activated when Stage1 is set to 1, putting my avatar in a 'ready mode' such as holding a gun, and then I have an animation when Stage2 is set to 1, which plays an automatic gunfire animation. Then, when Stage2 is set to 0, it goes back into 'ready mode'
Under the older button menu option, I could set a Submenu to set Stage1 to 1, and fill that submenu with a single button that sets Stage2 to 1. It would fire for as long as the trigger is held, and when released, stop firing.
This behavior no longer works since Button Behavior was changed. Regardless, the old system didn't have the same update rate, so it was never well suited for the example I provided above.
Another example of integer based puppet menu options that would be helpful is provided in the image.
Basically, a 'charge attack' animation plays for 3 seconds. If the button is released before the charge up is finished, the animation cancels and goes to its neutral state. If the button is held long enough for the charge up animation to finish, it moves to a looping 'full charge' animation and waits for the button to be released, then plays a new animation.
This worked (locally) under the older system as well, and is handy to prevent accidentally triggering larger disruptive animations.
title: [FEEDBACK] Allow Integer based puppet menus.

details:
I tried Avatars 3.0 recently, and the interface is really good, but there's one major problem which I think I have a solution for.
The problem is that if you're puppeteering something, like your facial gestures, or a tail or whatever, you can't move with that stick. 
Now, you can of course, walk around the room you're in to move about a bit, but not all of us have a large playspace.
To get to the point, what I propose is to allow the use of the trigger, which is the only button you can really access while also moving the stick, as a momentary button to quickly open the menu, move the stick around, and then release to lock the avatar in whatever facial gesture or pose you selected while in the menu.
I believe as the menu currently operates, it will keep the last menu section you were in active, so this setup would enable you to quickly switch between moving and puppeteering, which I think is an absolute necessity for this method of doing facial gestures to replace the current standard. Otherwise, I feel like avatars will suddenly become a lot less animated in the face, because people will be less inclined to go into the menu often if they have to hold down a button to open it, select the face pose, and then exit it again with another button press. That's simply too much effort compared to a finger point. But pulling the trigger and pushing up at the same time and releasing the trigger again... That's quick and easy to do on the fly.
Of couse this momentary trigger setup may not play nice with the push in a direction then click method of selecting menu items that you made optional, but with the "flick" option, it would work fine.
title: [FEEDBACK] Quick menu access

details:
Previously, buttons would send their value while held down. This was ideal for activating facial expressions, which could then be activated for just however long you want to show them; you could keep the menu open and show and hide facial expressions by selecting items with the stick.
However, now buttons activate for a fixed time - we no longer have a way to activate an expression by holding down a control. To some extent this can be emulated by using toggles or puppet menus, however this isn't ideal:
1. Toggles aren't ideal for mutually exclusive states; you have to make a second motion to disable the first before enabling the second expression, and if you forget, which one wins?
2. Puppet menus are best used for blending; it's difficult to precisely indicate more than four points on the two-axis puppet menus (vs eight on a regular expressions menu) and for cases where blending isn't desired they're not the correct control scheme.
Having an additional type of control which simply activates while the stick (or mouse) is held over it would resolve these issues.
title: [FEEDBACK] Please add an activate-when-held menu item type

details:
AV2 has blink_left, blink_right and lowerlid_left and lowerlid_right as separate shape-key names, and some avatars are supposed to conform to them (even if they are not effectively executed separately for the left and right).
However, AV3 provides only one "single" item per animation.
This is a mistake in terms of compatibility.
Two or more slots should be available to maintain compatibility. As a result, the AV3 configuration can be completed in Unity alone, without modifying the FBX.
In general, the fewer editing points, the better for both the creator and the user.
It's true that there are a lot of avatars that don't have a problem with shape keys because they don't care about left and right, but that's a different matter.
And while it's true that FBX is easy to edit, the less you have to edit, the better. If you have a lot of them, or sell them, you should feel that more so.
----

しかしながら，AV3では左右まとめた｢1つの｣項目しか用意されていません．
これは，互換性の観点で間違っていると言えるでしょう．
2スロット以上を用意し，互換性を保つべきと考えます．その結果，FBXに手を加えることなくUnity上だけでAV3の設定を完了可能になります．

title: [BUG] Debug Menu fails to show State names when the State Machine is named differently than the Layer.

comments.body: Fixed in 1005!
I can now happily say that of build 1005, this issue has been resolved. Feel free to mark this post as 'Complete' moderators!

I believe I may have found the origin of both this issue and why the same problem occurs upon entering Sub-State Machines.
Assuming that the developers are storing a map, table, or some other container that links the hashed name of a state to its actual name when the Avatar is built for later determining the name of a running state in-game using AnimatorStateInfo.fullPathHash, I think they may be incorrectly hashing the names.
There is little to no documentation from Unity about this as far as I'm aware, but the hashed value that AnimatorStateInfo.fullPathHash contains is a string containing the path of State Machines to the State (Ex. "<STATE_MACHINE>.<SUB_STATE_MACHINE>.<STATE>"), however some online forums mistakenly claimed that it was the name of the Layer and the State (Ex. "<LAYER>.<STATE>"). This is only true when there are no Sub-State Machines and the Layer's primary State Machine is named the same as the Layer. 
It's quite possible the developers saw one of these forum posts, implemented it this way by accident, and it never was noticed or no one cared to fix it. So instead, when the Debug menu fails to find the name of the State, it simply displays the hash value it received from AnimatorStateInfo.fullPathHash.
Do remember that this is all speculation though, I don't have access to the source code of VRChat after all. I did however manage to replicate this behavior with a few scripts in Unity perfectly as can be seen in the GIF, as well as what happens when the State Machine names are used for correctly hashing the State names instead.
EDIT: Turns out the Unity Documentation itself is also wrong about this. For the method IsName() within the AnimatorStateInfo class, it says to use the form *Layer.Name* when it actually needs to be using the State Machine names instead.

Ok, one final update on this topic.
I have managed to both find the place this mistake is located at within the VRCSDK builder code and have successfully fixed the debug menu myself.
My theory about the use of Layer names rather than State Machine names was correct. As can be seen within [this image](https://imgur.com/2VDVdBj), they use the Layer names when generating hashes and ignore Sub-State Machines entirely. This section of code can be found within "VRCSdkControlPanelAvatarBuilder.cs" at line 343 within the VRCSDK.
To fix it, I created a separate static class named AV3Hasher and put in a recursive method for hashing an entire State Machine properly. I then simply replaced the code within the foreach loop in the SDK with a call to this function. You can see an image of the class' structure [here](https://imgur.com/j6VKl4G) and how the code in the VRCSDK was changed [here](https://imgur.com/mdImWX7).
The Debug menu shows all State names correctly upon uploading an Avatar that uses Sub-State Machines and differently named State Machines after doing this modification, signifying that this entire issue can be completely resolved with an update to the SDK.
However, one thing I noticed when testing this fix is that any Layers that weren't customized (using defaults) will still be using incorrect hashes, meaning that the hashes for default layers are stored elsewhere and need to be updated as well.
If any VRChat developers are reading this and would like to incorporate this code into the SDK themselves, I've created a Unity Package  containing both the AV3Hasher class and the modified "VRCSdkControlPanelAvatarBuilder.cs" file that you can download [here](https://mega.nz/file/RQgH3LDL#Gmc0CPAZdWc0Sv5ZaARdM3hcCABzXG0oVPtmVoipELY).

details:
As it stand, the new 3.0 FBT feature exposes a major flaw with FBT: that your arm length and your height are assumed to be proportional to each other.
This leads to users such as myself being incorrectly scaled to their avatar. 
One way this defect manifests is when a user has to modify their real height to smaller than their actual height to have their FBT pose actually scaled correctly. In Avatar 3.0 this leads to the player floating above the ground, forcing the user to use a playspace moving tool to reposition themselves with their feet on the floor.
The solution to this is to gather more data about the player so that the FBT pose can be scaled correctly, via adding an arm span option in addition to a player height option. Otherwise, a fix for being forced to input an incorrect height setting and then floating would be to add a player offset option ingame so that a floating player can be moved back down to the ground in-game.
title: FBT: Add an arm length option in addition to user height.

details:
[Transrated]
In the current Expressions Menu, only the parameter to sync specified in the Expression Parameters can be operated.
Since there is a limit of up to 16 parameters to sync, it is wasteful to assign parameters to sync to operate from the Expressions Menu, even for things that do not need to be synced.
Examples of parameters that do not need to be synced are camera gimmicks that allow you to control depth of field and FoV.
This only needs to work in its own Local, and we think it is wasteful to consume sync parameters.
As a solution, we propose that you can operate parameters that are not specified in the Expression Parameters from the Expressions Menu.

details:
This idea is mainly for people who purchase SDK3 avatars from Booth, VKET, or other sources, but aren't very familiar with Unity on a whole.
For it to work the avatar descriptor would have a section where you can specify what parameters are active by default when you upload an avatar.
For example:
1) The user sets the avatar to always load in on the Green color scheme, as opposed to the default Blue.
2) The user sets the avatar to always load in on the dark skinned setting, rather than the light skinned one.
While you can just change the default layer state on the FX layer to do that, there is an issue where in game it will not realize the default layer has been switched. So in this case the hair and skintone are on the same material, and you attempted to switch the hair color in game, it will reset to the default skintone instead of your preferred one.
Specifying parameters through the descriptor means the game will understand that "skintone = 2" is active, and take that into account when choosing which hair color animation it switches to in game.
This will also make it easier for creators to optimize while still offering many options, as having separate materials for hair/eyes/skintone just to prevent this kind of thing from happening piles on the drawcalls quickly.
title: Allow the avatar descriptor to specify default SDK3 expression states on avatar upload.

details:
This is an Avatars 3.0 feature request.
As an avatar creator, I would like to be able to measure one or several distances between 2 transforms of my choosing.
Those distances would be calculated each frame and would be exposed to the playable layer animators.
An optional choice would be provided so that the measured distance in Unity units could be inverse lerped into a normalized distance between 0.0 and 1.0 based on a minimum and maximum distance that I would set in advance for that measurement.
Additionally, if at least one of the two transforms is disabled, then the measured distance is always 0.0.
By exposing a method to measure one or several distances on the avatar, I could make:
A: Pocket items. Measure the distance between the hand and a pocket. When the hand starts doing a fist gesture near that pocket by comparing the distance, the animator drives a synced boolean to put an item on that hand, making it seem like an object was just picked up from that pocket.
B: Clap hands particle without collider. Measure the distance between the two hands. In the FX layer, add a condition so that whenever the measured distance ends up below 0.3 units, a hands clap particle can be seen.
C: Distance-based emissive material. Read the distance between the hand and another object on the avatar, with a minimum distance of 0.2 and a maximum distance of 2. An animation with Normalized Time reads that normalized distance, and animates the color of a material, making it emissive as the hand becomes close to that object.
D: Velocity measurement. Every tenth of a second, two transforms are moved around alternatively based on the hand position. By measuring the distance between the two transforms, we can deduce the velocity of the hand, and play an effect based on that hand velocity.
E: Scale an object based on distance. In the Gesture layer, an animation with Normalized Time or a Blend Tree reads the normalized distance between the two hands in order to scale that object linearly.
title: [Feature request] Add an Avatars 3.0 component to measure the distance between two transforms

It was the base block for a lot of things I had. I don't want to go back to the pre SDK 3.0 era way of doing things with mega hacks, dropping performance, and not being able to synchronize stuff.
This should be a very light weight and simple solution that opens so many doors in avatar creation. It sucks having hands tied, this might not be usable directly by every avatar creator, but fortunately there are a ton of people that make prefab systems and tutorials that enables beginner avatar creators to take advantage of it.
I am sorry for this little rant, but I really wouldn't like something like this to fall in oblivion.

Just a small comment on a feature that could be added to that, is the ability to also measure the distance between the player with said transform.
Basicaly, if you only select a single transform, the value becomes the distance between You and said transform, adding interactivity with other players, playing animations when you touch someone for exemple (Slap!)

D isn't so clean because the velocity of a transform will be different over the network than it is locally, when driven by tracker/IK motion, and you have to roughly compensate for that in your animator design-- something that I wish wouldn't be a concern for a velocity measuring system. That said, I think this is an elegant approach that achieves completely replacing what was lost in the last patch, while also opening up new options.

I want to make clear for the purpose of this canny, this is to solve **interactions with my own avatar**, and I think proposal will work great for self interactions while still providing enough . If we want to discuss **cross player interactions**, that would *best* be done by a separate proposal, but not sure what such a proposal would look like exactly.
@{5b07ba05a954d760abc336d4|full_name}: you would still be able to achieve your effects in this canny using particles as before: old style stop action effect systems can *still* be used with this proposal when absolutely needed. However, with this canny, the performance overhead of the extra particle system is no longer required except for things that really need particle collision detection. details:
When other players load an avatar faster than the avatar wearer, the avatar's Expression Parameters can have unintended values from the perspective of those who have loaded the avatar.
This may cause the animator to execute remotely in a way that was not designed by the avatar author.
For instance, when all of the following are combined:
- the avatar have pieces of clothing enabled by default in the hierarchy
- the animator states are entering a default state that makes sure they are enabled on entry
- the expression parameters has a default value properly set in a way that the entry state will not transition to another state unless manually acted upon
...even when all of these conditions are satisfied, when the other players load the avatar faster than the wearer, then the Expression Parameters may be seen by others with an unintended value that is non-default, causing the animator to transition to other states after loading, which may disable said clothing.
This kind of behavior is invisible to the avatar wearer who may never be aware that this is happening. It puts a lot of burden onto the avatar creator to handle this edge case properly.
title: [Bug] When other players load an avatar faster than the avatar wearer, the expression parameters can have unintended values which may cause clothes to disappear for a split second

details:
Currently, the AFK animation must be triggered manually by desktop players. For VR Players, afk happens naturally when the headset is removed or within the SteamVR Menu. Somebody who is unavailable in VR is unambiguously unavailable because they will trigger one of these two things.
However, Desktop players who don't hit the End key and abandon their keyboard will stare off into space indefinitely, the AFK animation never triggering, meaning that it's possible to appear standing, but not be actively playing or speaking.
title: [FEEDBACK] Auto-AFK desktop players after a period of In-activity

comments.body: As a thought, what about users who are sitting there and watching a video for a long period of time? I don't think you'd want to trigger AFK for them, and you don't want to force them to wiggle their mouse every few minutes, or have to set an option that they didn't have to set before. 🤔

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: I kinda left the definition of in-activity kinda vague specifically because of this. It's definitely not a simple suggestion. Even if you did something like say, check for microphone activity, that both excludes those who choose to play mute and can be accidentally circumvented by those who have overly sensitive microphones.
One might consider setting 'AFK time' in the settings menu at a default value of 'don't auto AFK', in order for the user to AFK or not on their own agency. I think everybody values the AFK function differently based on if they've made a custom animation for it or not. Additionally, the idea of making it its very own setting means that it can change with the user's context. This may fall into the definition of 'setting an option', however, so another concept.
To determine when to turn someone AFK or not, we should first have a definition for what 'activity' and 'inactivity' looks like in a way it's reasonable to measure. Some examples of in-activity could be:
-Keeping the Window out of focus is a good measure if someone is paying attention to the game. Best case scenario, the user has moved attention fully to something else, and most iffy scenario, the user may have tabbed over to another program for a short time. For example, going back and forth between blender/unity and the game to check how their avatar functions and what tweaks to make. Of course, currently, SteamVR overlay also triggers the animation, so it'd be a similar case as the current VR example.
-Far proximity from other users. A player not within a certain distance to another player is most likely not actually active. If a desktop is watching a video with a group of other players, it's still possible they're participating. Proximity to video players most likely won't work as a metric since every world is different and while some worlds have close up tv sized video players, others have far off movie theater sized video players.
Now, some things that I think are unambiguously activity.
-Moving is a certain way of proving the player is active, and I don't think I need to do any convincing there.
-Mic activity, as mentioned earlier, could be a bad option due to the presence of unusually sensitive microphones, and people who prefer to play mute. But in the case of push to talk, that press can be used as a definite way to ensure someone is currently active. If you want mic activity to be the deciding factor rather than just PTT, you could change how much mic activity is necessary to ward off the AFK state. Maybe little blips don't count, but full on seconds of activity do.
You could assign multiple cases of 'suggested inactivity' and have a different time threshold for each. Someone tabbing out for more than 10 seconds should be considered afk, Someone not moving, AND not speaking, AND not around anybody else can probably have a timer for 5 minutes. Somebody not moving, but with other people who are also active could probably have a much more generous limit, maybe 10-15 minutes. I personally find it hard to believe that someone could be in-game and unintentionally not move or speak at all for 10-15 minutes at a time to accidentally trigger the afk state, but if it's too much of a big deal, you could instead just have it so that the AFK state cannot be initiated while in proximity of one other 'active' player. Maybe put players in a 'soft AFK' state where the parameter doesn't change until they're out of proximity with other active players.
This turned into a wall of text fast, but in general, there's not real one single perfect solution to that problem you mention, but I think there's some reasonable workaround solutions.

@{5c4bd9bca31c1d6ef9355351|full_name}: For force afk, you could have a animation that go really slow then transfer to another state when not moving. That state set a bool to go in a duplicate afk branch that don't disable locomotion with a condition that detect if you move any velocity to get out.

details:
In Unity Editor, modified Parameter Drivers Behaviors are not saved to disk if it's the last modification of the animator.
If such a modification is made, an avatar can be uploaded with a modified VRC Avatar Parameter Driver that contains the new values, but as soon as Unity Editor is closed then opened again, then uploading the same avatar will result in a VRC Avatar Parameter Driver that contains the previous values.
Use case:
I tried to tweak driver values between multiple avatar uploads in order to encode parameter presets, and then uploading the avatar. However, reuploading the avatar again the next day with tweaked materials without touching the animator resulted in different driver parameters values being applied.
How to reproduce:
- Using VRCSDK3-AVATAR-2021.02.23.11.41_Public.unitypackage
- Open Unity
- Create a new animator controller
- Open the Animator editor
- In the Parameters tab, Create a new float parameter
- Add a State in the base layer
- Add a VRC Avatar Parameter Driver behavior to that state
- Add a Parameter to that VRC Avatar Parameter Driver
- Set the value to 0.5
- Close Unity Editor
- Start Unity Editor
- Open the Animator editor
- Click the state
- Set the value to 0.7
- Do not change anything else in the animator, including moving a state around or hitting CTRL-S
- * See additional footnotes
- Close Unity Editor
- Start Unity Editor
- Open the Animator editor

details:
I like to go exploring. It's cool to find interesting random worlds not many people know about. However, sometimes you run into worlds that were not very well made--for example, they might be too poorly lit for my headset and eyesight (or for everyone's). In order to be able to see at all in those worlds, I want to include some sort of flashlight or other light source in my avatars.
This will immediately cause my avatars to be marked as "Poor" performance. Even though the light source in my avatar is toggleable, disabled by default. And, sure, I can understand how realtime lighting can multiply performance woes in a busy world. But there's a matter here of what the performance system is trying to accomplish and what it's actually accomplishing.
Let's see. I'm presented with a choice. I can either not include the light source and lose functionality that's important to me, or I can take the performance rating of "Poor" and assume that the vast majority of people will still see my avatar, and those who don't by default are more than well trained (by custom and circumstance) to unblock it. Since I'm not actually causing any performance degradation by including an inactive light, I have no moral qualms with choosing option A.
But now, here's the rub. My avatar has a "poor" rating, no matter how efficient it is in all of the other categories. What incentive do I have to make it performant (better than "Poor", at least), in any of them? Other than a sense of duty and willingness to make everyone's experience better, very little. It's hard work to make an avatar that's both good and performant. If I've already been punished in advance for poor performance, and any user of the avatar will be restricted anyway--it's only natural to assume that anyone who does see my "poor" avatar has accepted the risk of a "poor" performance avatar in the first place, since they have configured their client to show it--I'm much more incentivized to make an avatar that's cooler and more functional, even if it's less performant.
It wouldn't be so bad if this issue was specific to light sources, but no. That is far from the only perverse incentive in the system. The performance system has all the delicacy of a sledgehammer. All particle systems cost 2 material slots--regardless of whether they're actually used. But material source animations cost 0. All audio sources are treated equally, no matter how long, loud, high range or otherwise intrusive they are.
The v3 workflow of using menus and animations to control parameters of an avatar is directly at odds with the performance system, because it encourages--sometimes requires--the subdivision of the avatar into more meshes, more materials, etc. in order to permit their fine grained control... For toggles, there's the trick of putting the prop on a bone in the main avatar and scaling the bone down to 0, which I imagine is *less* performant than disabling the prop entirely, especially if the prop is complex (because the prop is still being rendered). For blendtrees, it turns out that animations can't control specific materials in a mesh, only every material at the same time, so instead of a mesh with multiple materials, I'm encouraged to have more meshes. 
I could use a custom shader to overcome this issue. But if I use a custom shader and the shader is blocked by the viewer's trust level, which is likely, the avatar might show incorrectly or broken. Sure, if the amount of meshes bumps the avatar into a worse performance rating, maybe the avatar won't show at all for a specific user. But if it does, it will show correctly, since I will be using standard shaders instead. And if the user can't see me at all--and a lot of others--they're much more incentivized to change things on their side in order to become capable of seeing us. If they see *something*, they have less of an incentive to do anything. And who wants to unblock shaders for everyone? The shaders some people use are way more obnoxious than any avatars marked poor performance but which don't necessarily perform that bad. By reasoning like this, I am, once again, incentivized to worsen my avatar's rating.
I want to suggest two key changes to the performance system in order to remove most of its perverse incentives and make it more sane for avatar makers to work with:
1. Make it point based. So for each category, "excellent", "good", etc. would be worth a certain amount of (polynomially increasing) points. Then add all the points together and use that value to determine the final performance rating of the avatar, using linear thresholds. It's not that complicated if the SDK control panel is doing all the work, and this means a single bad category doesn't entirely invalidate the performance optimization work of all the others. If certain categories are more important to you than others, just make them worth more points, but converselly account for the external incentives to use the thing in that category, too.
2. Dig deeper into components when determining the performance classification for each category. The system already does some digging in order to find how many materials are being used, etc. It would be nice it, for example, avatar makers were rewarded for objects that start inactive, or shorter and quieter audio.
title: [FEEDBACK] The perverse incentives in the performance/safety systems

details:
Currently synced custom paremeters consume either 1 or 8 bits out of the 128 bit total available for each avatar. If I store my selectors as Ints, I feel like I have enough ideas per avatar to easily exceed this limit.

But some selectors don't necessarily require 8 bits of storage. For example, if I have 8 facial expressions, I could encode that information in only 3 bits. That means my Int parameter is wasting 5 bits, which could easily contain another selector or maybe a bunch of toggles. If I have at least 2 low count selectors in my avatar, I can kind of do this by having a single "Command" or "Macro" Int parameter for the menu to set, where each position represents an unrelated command, then encode everything else using Bools and drive the Bools with parameter drivers. But that's an unnecessarily cumbersome method and also breaks my ability to use Toggle controls in the menu (or, in other words, to display state).

The easiest solution for this problem would be for the SDK to provide shorter integers as synced parameter types for storage. At least 2 and 4 bit integers, although due to the size of radial menus I feel like 3 bits would be extremely useful too. In the playable layers, all of these would be translated into regular "ints", but truncated if their value exceeds their capacity when being synced or stored.

The idea in https://feedback.vrchat.com/avatar-30/p/feedback-control-the-not-sync-parameters-from-expressions-menu also mitigates this problem (though it's worse), since it would allow local variables in the menus to display state and integrate features in a more human-friendly manner. It would still require encoding into Bool parameters to be performed with parameter drivers, though.

Another great way to solve insufficient storage woes would be to give VRC+ users the ability to store 256 bits per avatar (as the uploader). Seems like the sort of thing people would actually pay for.
title: [FEEDBACK] Improvements in synced custom parameter storage

details:
This is a follow up to the following cannies:
- [BUG] VRC Avatar Parameter Driver does not work for a few frames after avatar loading https://vrchat.canny.io/avatar-30/p/bug-vrc-avatar-parameter-driver-does-not-work-for-a-few-frames-after-avatar-load
- [Bug] When other players load an avatar faster than the avatar wearer, the expression parameters can have unintended values which may cause clothes to disappear for a split second https://vrchat.canny.io/avatar-30/p/bug-when-other-players-load-an-avatar-faster-than-the-avatar-wearer-the-expressi
As an avatar creator, I would like to know when the Avatars 3.0 system is loaded and ready to go, so that I can execute state machines that are sensitive to avatar loading conditions at the right moment.
My proposal is to add a new bool parameter that is True whenever Avatars 3.0 is ready to function.
When that parameter is True, then the Avatar creator can assume that the following assertions are true:
- When true, it should be assumed that Avatars 3.0 system has successfully loaded for the person who is wearing the avatar, even in the case when other players load the avatar faster than the avatar wearer.
- When true, it should be assumed that all of the Expression Parameters of the newly loaded avatar have synced at least once with the expected values for remote players -- that is, that bool remained false for as long as the avatar wearer has not loaded the avatar yet nor synced the correct Expression Parameter values.
- When true, it should be assumed that Animator Behaviors such as Drivers are going to work properly once we enter a new state that has one.
- When true, it should be assumed that Animator Parameters like IsLocal, VRMode, TrackingType have a defined and stable values that are unlikely going to change afterwards.
This may help solve the following cases for avatar creators:
- On some logic layers, this allows evaluating the rest of the state machine at the right moment, triggering Driver behaviors (i.e. random number generators, etc.).
- On some layers, this could allow a temporary stopgate in order to enter the correct state machine that matches the user's TrackingType and VRMode.
- If a layer needs to handle the case where Expression Parameters have a default value that is not 0 or that is not false, this prevents the animator from carrying on until the Expression Parameters have been synced by the avatar wearer.
This also avoids having to wait for an unreliable arbitrary number of frames.
title: [Feature request] Add a bool parameter that is true if Avatars 3.0 Parameters and Behaviors are ready to be executed, and the Avatar Wearer has loaded and synced their Expression Parameters

details:
I've discussed this on discord in the past but never made an official request, so here it goes.

I'd like to have the concept of object unions in the avatars SDK. The avatar creator would be able to create (and register in an array in the descriptor) a "union": a set of gameobjects from the avatar's hierarchy. VRChat would then guarantee that at most only one object from each set is enabled at a time. If more than one is enabled during loading all but the first enabled objects would be automatically disabled. If an object in the set is toggled active and another object in the set was already enabled, it would be automatically disabled.

When calculating avatar performance, the SDK would examine every object in each set but only add the polygons, bones, material, etc. from the heaviest object in the set, rather than the sum of all of them, to the weight of each independent criterion. This would result in a much more accurate representation of the performance cost of avatars with mutually exclusive props or clothing and keep creators from using tricks that can, under certain circumstances, result in higher real performance costs, difficult to maintain projects or unexpected results (such as broken shadows).

An expansion of this system would also allow VRChat client users to be given the ability to more intelligently restrict avatar features for performance gains by adding a toggle to explicitly tag a union as "clothing" - a set of alternative versions of the same item (or items with the same purpose). Then instead of a simple on/off toggle for avatars in the safety tab, the user could have a performance slider: "Best, Good, Medium," etc. If VRChat deemed that a certain object belonging to a "clothing" set exceeds the performance limiter set by the viewer, the avatar would (locally) fall back on the highest alternative from the clothing set that respects the performance setting, and would only hide the avatar if all alternatives were too heavy to respect the performance setting.
title: [FEEDBACK] Sets/Unions

details:
A lot of avatars don't have realistic proportions, as such, by stretching the arms IRL it is possible to reach farther than the avatar can. I propose a way to automatically scale the arm bones (on the local axis) to mitigate this problem.
Some people prefer the look of taller legs and shorter arms, this is why I request 2 different systems, to account for both cases:
- System #1 (Passive) - Avatars are scaled as they are in the present, however, if the user is able to reach farther than the avatar at some angles the arm bones are stretched to accommodate for the user being able to do so temporarily.
- System #2 (Toggle) - A new option is created called "Realistic Avatar Proportions" which modifies the avatar's arm-span to make them realistically proportionate to the avatar's height, similar to human proportions. This is for those that don't mind changing an avatar's proportions to match their own, eliminating floor-level mismatch.
The first system can be used simultaneously with the second one (in case the shoulders are weirdly positioned).
Arguments against:
- Human bones don't stretch IRL, it would be weird to do that in-game.
Yes, they don't. However, the arms only need to be scaled by a small percentage and still make a huge difference in terms of proportions. At this scale it is not noticeable, way less than the avatar not being able to stretch its arms forward to match your controller's position.
- I like the look of my avatar, I don't want to change the proportions.
This is why I proposed both systems. One as a toggle that changes the avatar proportions to realistic ones and another one that just passively accommodates with less effect.
Possible implementations:
- The bones need to be scaled along the local axis and not moved. By moving the wrist bones it messes with avatars that have separate meshes(ex: robotic joints, etc) Properly stretching the arm bones instead of moving them fixes this problem.
title: [FEEDBACK] Option to scale arm bones to combat bad proportions

details:
This is a collection of perceived bugs from ever since the interval version of FinalIK got updated/Avatar 3 released. I know I am very late to be posting this stuff, but I have been very annoyed noticing these differences all this time considering I am a very old player from when VRC used Unity 5.6. The issues I am outlining affect SDK2 and SDK3 Humanoid avatars unless specified otherwise.
- Control being passed back to the VRIK component is considerably delayed (~3-5 seconds) after stopping locomoting even when all layers of every PlayableLayer have stopped transitioning. This is very noticeable by looking at the LowerBody (especially the feet) when in TrackingType < 6 and coming to a full stop when locomoting.
- (SDK3) Auto-footstepping is only enabled when Upright > 0.7 (Even if the active state is the standing state).
- Jumping seems to lock the LowerBody to the idle pose instead of control being retained by the VRIK component even if no Animator Tracking Control components are affecting any LowerBody field. (this was tested on Desktop. The effect is subtle, but noticeable and causes LowerBody IK such as auto-footstepping to be disabled for ~3-5 seconds)
- (This should be done with default PlayableLayers for a noticeable effect) Switching to an SDK2 avatar from an SDK3 avatar partially retains the Locomotion Animator layer. This is easily observable by being in a TrackingType of 6 (FBT) and jumping while sitting down. The expected behavior is that the legs should continue to retain tracking to the feet trackers. What actually happens is they're forced into the idle pose while "tracking control is set to animation". I surround that in quotes because that concept theoretically should not exist to SDK2 avatars and does not exist if the user loads into a scene in an SDK2 avatar. Transitioning scenes while in an SDK2 avatar fixes this issue.

details:
As we cannot use our own scripts in VRChat, we're limited by what's whitelisted for components. Which is largely built-in Unity ones for anything not very specific to and made by VRChat. The Rotation Constraint component built into Unity, along with the Translation/Scale/Parent components, operate at relative angles to what the two objects orientations are in the Unity editor regardless of what the axis of the constrained object is. Not simply taking axis movement and directly copy/pasting that amount of movement to the constrained axis.
Now, for certain behaviours, this is perfectly fine. Mandatory/preferable over direct-axis translation to the other axis even in many cases. And for those cases, how things are now is amazing, as the maths required to be able to rotate something based on the arbitrary axis of the source object instead of simply copying values to the corresponding axis is incredibly difficult. The problem is, when you DON'T want that behaviour and want to be able to just go “X axis on the first object moves X axis on the other constrained object Y amount.”
To script this as a component is dead easy (It's literally taking the change in rotation/position/scale of one object and pasting that difference to the other object) to create, hence the reason that is not a built-in component in Unity. We cannot use our own scripts though, making such things impossible in VRChat.
So my proposal is,
A new set of component types that come with the VRC-SDK called “Direct Rotation Constraint”, with Translation/Scale/Parent equivalents. Operating in a similar fashion to the existing constraints, except it makes it's changes based on the local axis of the individual objects instead of relative to the axis of the source object(s) like the existing constraints do now.
Which from an interface standpoint is nearly identical and has all the same options (So ability to set multiple objects to be sources with weights, position/rotation/scale at rest, lock axis, etc.) the Unity native one has, except with two key additional options:
> The ability to set which axis of the source object(s) affect the axis of the constrained object. For example, you want the rotation of the Y axis of the source object to change the Z axis of the constrained object instead of the Y axis of the constrained object. I imagine a interface of the three axis of the source on one side of a box with the 3 axis of the constrained object on the other, and being able to connect axis together like you would with connecting the nodes of the Udon Node script system.
> The ability to invert the effects of axis. So if a object is rotated +12 degrees on the axis that's driving the rotation constrained axis, it would rotate that constrained axis -12 degrees instead. Easiest thing would be to have that as a toggle next to the constrained axis column with the previously described node-connect method of setting which axis affects what. 
All of that was a very long winded way of describing something that should be incredibly simple if implemented, and would make previous functionally previously literally impossible now possible. For example, fingers on bat wings actually drivable by a humanoid rig as bat fingers need to be off-axis to look right. And duplicate arms being able to be off-axis from the source real arms, meaning they won't look as blatantly obvious they're constrained together. And far, far more examples I'm sure I can't even think of.
Thank you for any consideration, and I hope to see a time when avatar and world customization is extended to being able to do even more crazy things with an addition that in the grand scheme of things is incredibly simple.
title: [FEEDBACK] Constraints with Axis Driven Directly instead of only Relative

details:
There seems to be an issue where your mirror reflection clone does not behave as expected with regards to layer weights changed by the animator layer control behaviour for animations in that layer that involve material swap and material settings. I am not entirely certain when this issue started happening, but it was not observed to effect my avatars when physbones was released to live. As material swaps and material property animations are only supposed to happen on the FX layer, I would assume this bug only affects the FX layer.

I've reproduced the problem in this avatar id : avtr_56d9d511-2f9e-4ba0-b33a-c06c81f1497b

There are 2 layers in this avatar labled SphereGreen and SphereRed respectively on the FX controller.

The avatar has a coloured sphere in front of it

SphereGreen has a single animation that 
- Sets the colour of the sphere to green via material colour property
- Sets the size of the sphere to a scale of 0.1
- Disables a second sphere green in colour

SphereRed has a single animation that
- Sets the colour of the sphere to red via material colour property
- Sets the size of the sphere to a scale of 0.5
- Enables a second sphere green in colour

Write defaults are off.

The layer weights of SphereGreen and SphereRed are set to 1

SphereGreen is layer 4 while SphereRed is layer 5, as such SphereRed's animation should take priority if the layer weight is not 0.

SphereGreen has an animator layer control behaviour that sets SphereRed layer weight to 0.
Expected behaviour: 
- sphere is green for local, remote players, and mirror reflection.
Outcome: 
- sphere is green for local and remote players, but is red in mirror reflection.

The size of the sphere and the toggling of the second sphere are behaving as expected.
The above was also tested using material swaps to the same result.

To be clear, if the layer weight of SphereRed was set to 0 by default and not via the avatar layer control behaviour, it behaves as expected.

The inverse is also true, if SphereRed was initially set to a weight of 0 and set to 1 via an avatar layer control behaviour, the mirror reflection has a green sphere instead of an expected red sphere.

As you can see in the screenshot, the layer weight for SphereRed is 0, and the sphere for my player local avatar is green, but the sphere in the mirror reflection is red.
title: [BUG][1203,1204] Mirror reflection clone does not respect layer weights changed by the animator layer control for animations involving material swaps and material settings
